title: A Tiny Lip Point in 'Forgotten Island' Says a Lot
summary:
In DreamWorks' new animated film 'Forgotten Island', one tiny moment has become famous online: the lip point. At a goodbye party for Raissa Molina, who is heading to Caltech, her best friend Jo arrives late and asks where Raissa is. An older woman points with her lips.

People who know Filipino culture spotted it at once, and so did many Latino fans.

The moment was in the script from the very first draft, director Joel Crawford told IndieWire. The filmmakers wanted to draw on their own experience of Filipino culture. 'Growing up around Filipinos, the lip point was something that was so specific and unique to me,' Crawford said. Adding it felt like a celebration, he said, and it made the characters feel real.

Later in the film, Jo does it herself. The film has a Filipino cast and a cultural consultant. Jo's hand movements were based on skater Margie Didal, and the villain Manananggal's movements drew on dancer Phil Tayag.

Most of the story takes place on the island of Nakali, home to magical creatures, and the pictures draw on 1990s Filipino art and anime. That small detail became a symbol of how the film shows Filipino culture.
why_it_matters: It shows you how a tiny detail from real life can make a story feel true and help people see their own culture on screen.
